mainTopic: Bird offerings killed and offered outside the עזרה, which case רבי שמעון is arguing about, and a new משנה on placing the blood of a חטאת, from one cup or two, outside.
overview: This amud finishes the משנה about bird offerings (עוף) that are killed and then offered up outside the עזרה. The proper way to kill a bird קרבן inside is מליקה (pinching), while שחיטה inside ruins it; slaughtering it outside and offering it outside, though, makes one חייב. The משנה sums up these rules, and רבי שמעון adds a general rule with one exception. The גמרא first fixes the word 'הכשירו' to 'חיובו', since שחיטה of a bird is not its preparation. It then asks which ruling רבי שמעון is arguing with and tests the cases of the משנה against his exact wording, rejecting each one. זעירי says the argument is about slaughtering an animal at night, and רבא says it is about collecting blood in a non-sacred vessel. Finally, a ברייתא shows that רבי שמעון makes pinching outside liable, so the גמרא reads his words as referring to the pinching case. A new משנה then teaches when placing the blood of a חטאת outside brings liability, with one cup or two. It compares this to a person who has two animals set aside for one חטאת.

steps.title: Slaughtering a bird outside and offering it outside
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that if one slaughtered a bird קרבן outside the עזרה and then offered it up outside, he is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he slaughtered the bird outside and offered it up outside, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the last case in its list of bird cases: the bird was slaughtered outside and also offered up outside, and the person is חייב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Inside the עזרה, a bird is meant to be killed by מליקה, not שחיטה. Outside the עזרה, however, slaughtering a bird and offering it up does make one חייב for offering a קרבן outside.

keyTerms.meaning: He slaughtered (cut the throat with a knife)
He offered it up (burned it as a קרבן)
Pinching the bird's neck with the כהן's fingernail, the proper way to kill a bird קרבן

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with an animal קרבן. For a bird, שחיטה is not the proper way to kill it inside the Temple, yet slaughtering it outside still makes one חייב.

phrases.english: If he slaughtered a bird offering outside
and offered it up outside, he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of bird cases from before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Slaughtering a bird outside and offering it outside makes one חייב.

steps.title: The משנה sums up the bird rules
steps.stepSummary: The משנה draws a rule from its cases: the proper act inside (מליקה) brings exemption when done outside, and the act done outside (שחיטה) brings exemption when done inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: It turns out: the way it is prepared inside brings its exemption outside, and the way it is prepared outside brings its exemption inside.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה wraps up all the bird cases into one neat two-sided rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מליקה is the proper act inside, so doing it outside does not make a real קרבן, and offering it outside is פטור. שחיטה is the act that makes one חייב outside, but doing it inside ruins the bird, so offering it afterward outside is פטור. The משנה calls שחיטה the 'preparation' outside, and the גמרא will question that word.

keyTerms.meaning: The way it is made fit or proper

steps.whatToRemember: For a bird: מליקה inside is proper and שחיטה inside ruins it. Outside, שחיטה makes one חייב and מליקה does not.

phrases.aramaic: נִמְצָא דֶּרֶךְ הֶכְשֵׁירוֹ בִּפְנִים – פְּטוּרוֹ בַּחוּץ,
phrases.english: It turns out: the manner of its preparation inside brings its exemption outside,
phrases.notes: The preparation inside is מליקה, so pinching the bird outside leaves one exempt.

phrases.english: and the manner of its preparation outside brings its exemption inside.
phrases.notes: The act outside is שחיטה, so slaughtering inside and then offering outside leaves one exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sums up the case in step 1 together with the earlier bird cases into one rule.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whatever is proper inside exempts when done outside, and whatever obligates outside exempts when done inside.

steps.title: רבי שמעון's general rule and its one exception
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says that any killing which makes one חייב for offering outside when done outside also makes one חייב when done inside and then offered outside. The exception is slaughtering a bird inside and offering it outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: anything for which one is liable when it is done outside, one is liable for something similar done inside and then offered outside, except one who slaughters a bird inside and offers it outside.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון gives a broad general rule about killing inside versus outside. He makes one exception: a bird slaughtered inside and offered outside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His rule says that if a certain killing done outside leads to liability, the same killing done inside and then offered outside also leads to liability. The only case he takes out of this rule is שחיטה of a bird inside, which matches the first משנה's ruling of פטור.

keyTerms.meaning: Something similar to it, the same kind of act

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
Any act of killing for which, when done outside, one is liable for offering it up outside,
one is also liable for a similar act done inside
that he then offered up outside;
except for one who slaughters a bird inside
and offers it up outside; he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: כֹּל שֶׁחַיָּיבִין עָלָיו בַּחוּץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי שמעון's own general rule after the first משנה's summary.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Liability for a killing done outside carries over to the same killing done inside and then offered outside, except a bird slaughtered inside.

steps.title: The גמרא questions the word 'preparation'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the משנה can call שחיטה of a bird outside its 'הכשירו' (proper preparation). It is really what makes one liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: This word 'its preparation'?! It is its liability!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by challenging a word in the משנה's summary. Calling slaughter outside the bird's 'preparation' seems wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שחיטה does not make a bird קרבן proper; in fact it ruins it. What שחיטה outside really does is make the person חייב. So the word 'הכשירו' does not fit the second half of the summary.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
Its liability, what makes one חייב

phrases.english: GEMARA: This word, 'its preparation'?!
phrases.notes: This points back to the second half of the summary, 'דרך הכשירו מבחוץ', which is talking about שחיטה.

phrases.english: It is the reason for its liability!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the משנה's summary in step 2 and questions its wording.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שחיטה does not make a bird fit. It only causes liability outside, so calling it 'preparation' is inaccurate.

steps.title: Fix the wording to 'its liability'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees with the challenge and corrects the משנה to read 'חיובו' (its liability).
steps.simpleTranslation: Teach: 'its liability.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the question and simply fixes the word in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of defending 'הכשירו', the גמרא changes the reading. Now the summary says that what brings liability outside (שחיטה) brings exemption when done inside.
steps.whatToRemember: The summary now reads: the proper act inside (מליקה) exempts outside, and the act that obligates outside (שחיטה) exempts inside.

phrases.english: Teach: 'its liability.'
phrases.notes: The גמרא is changing the word in the משנה, so read 'דרך חיובו מבחוץ' instead of 'דרך הכשירו'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4 by correcting the text.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Text correction: the word in the משנה is changed.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה called שחיטה outside the bird's 'preparation'.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה should read 'חיובו', since שחיטה outside only causes liability.

steps.title: Which clause is רבי שמעון responding to?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי שמעון's words in the משנה and asks which earlier ruling he is arguing with.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says, etc. Which part of the משנה is he referring to?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new discussion about רבי שמעון's statement in the משנה. It asks which ruling of the תנא קמא he is reacting to. This question sets up the next several steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון's rule is general: any killing that brings liability when done outside also brings liability when done inside and offered outside. The גמרא wants to find the exact case where he disagrees with the תנא קמא. To do that, it will test each clause against his precise wording.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'on what does he stand?' It means: which statement is he referring to?
Etc. The rest of the quote is understood.
The first, unnamed opinion in the משנה

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says, etc.
To what is he referring?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the correction of the wording ('חיובו') to a new question about רבי שמעון's statement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which clause of the משנה רבי שמעון is disagreeing with.

steps.title: First try: he argues on the first clause and says pinching outside is also liable
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי שמעון refers to the רישא about מליקה. On this reading he says that pinching outside brings liability, just like pinching inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say he refers to the first clause: one who pinches a bird inside and offers it outside is liable, and one who pinches outside and offers outside is exempt. Then רבי שמעון would be saying: just as inside he is liable, outside too he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a first possible answer. Maybe רבי שמעון is arguing on the case of מליקה done outside, and he holds that it is also liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רישא has two halves. מליקה done inside and then offered outside is liable. מליקה done outside and then offered outside is exempt. On this reading רבי שמעון takes the liable inside case as his model and extends liability to the outside case.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say. It introduces a suggestion that will be tested.
The first clause of the משנה
Pinching the back of a bird's neck. This is the proper way to kill a bird קרבן.

phrases.english: If you say he is referring to the first clause:
One who pinches a bird inside
and offered it up outside is liable;
if he pinched outside and offered up outside, he is exempt.
And Rabbi Shimon said to him:
phrases.notes: 'Him' means the תנא קמא, the first opinion in the משנה.

phrases.english: Just as inside he is liable,
outside too he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a first possible answer to the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי שמעון refers to the רישא and holds that מליקה done outside is also liable.

steps.title: Rejected: his wording would have started from the inside case
steps.stepSummary: If רבי שמעון were extending liability from inside to outside, he would have said 'anything one is liable for inside.' He actually said 'outside.'
steps.simpleTranslation: But he says 'anything one is liable for outside'?! He should have said 'anything one is liable for inside'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the first suggestion because it does not match רבי שמעון's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a rule of the form 'just as X, so too Y,' X is the case that already brings liability. Under this reading X is the inside case, so his rule should begin 'כל שחייבין עליו בפנים.' Since his rule begins with 'בחוץ,' this reading does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: Anything one is liable for. These are the opening words of רבי שמעון's rule.

phrases.english: This [he says]: 'anything one is liable for outside'?!
He should have said: 'anything one is liable for inside'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The reading that רבי שמעון makes מליקה done outside liable
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That reading would require his rule to begin with 'בפנים,' not 'בחוץ.'

steps.title: Second try: he argues on the first clause and says pinching inside is also exempt
steps.stepSummary: Still within the רישא, the גמרא suggests the opposite direction. Just as מליקה outside is exempt, מליקה inside should also be exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, perhaps: just as outside he is not liable, inside too he should not be liable?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the same clause the other way around. Maybe רבי שמעון disagrees with the liable inside case and says it is also exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the model is the exempt outside case, and רבי שמעון would carry that exemption over to the inside case. This reverses the direction of step 7 but stays with the case of מליקה.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It introduces a new attempt.
He should be liable. With לָא, it means he should not be liable.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא כִּי הֵיכִי דִּבְחוּץ לָא מִיחַיַּיב,
phrases.english: Rather, just as outside he is not liable,
inside too he should not be liable?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא כִּי הֵיכִי דִּבְחוּץ לָא מִיחַיַּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 8 rejects the first reading, this offers another reading of the same clause.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי שמעון refers to the רישא and holds that מליקה done inside and offered outside is exempt.

steps.title: Rejected: his wording would have said 'not liable'
steps.stepSummary: If רבי שמעון were extending an exemption, his rule would begin 'anything one is NOT liable for outside.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Then he should have said 'anything one is not liable for outside'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the second suggestion because רבי שמעון's rule talks about liability, not exemption.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the model case is an exemption, the rule would have to say 'כל שאין חייבין עליו בחוץ.' רבי שמעון actually said 'כל שחייבין,' so he is extending liability, not exemption.

keyTerms.meaning: That one is not liable for

phrases.english: This [should have been]: 'anything one is not liable for outside'
he should have said!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי כֹּל שֶׁאֵין חַיָּיבִין עָלָיו בַּחוּץ מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The reading that רבי שמעון exempts מליקה done inside
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: His rule speaks of liability ('שחייבין'), not exemption ('שאין חייבין').

steps.title: Third try: he argues on the last clause and says slaughtering outside is exempt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי שמעון refers to the סיפא about שחיטה. On this reading he holds that שחיטה outside is exempt, just like שחיטה inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he refers to the last clause: one who slaughters a bird inside and offers it outside is exempt, and one who slaughters outside and offers outside is liable. Then רבי שמעון would be saying: just as inside he is not liable, outside too he is not liable.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the רישא did not work, the גמרא tries the סיפא. Maybe רבי שמעון disagrees with the liable outside case of שחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the סיפא, שחיטה done inside and offered outside is exempt, and שחיטה done outside and offered outside is liable. On this reading רבי שמעון takes the exempt inside case as his model and carries the exemption over to the outside case.

keyTerms.meaning: The last clause of the משנה
Slaughtering with a knife. For a bird קרבן this is not the proper method.

phrases.english: Rather, he is referring to the last clause:
One who slaughters a bird inside
and offered it up outside is exempt.
If he slaughtered outside and offered up outside, he is liable.
And Rabbi Shimon said to him:
Just as inside he is not liable,
outside too he is not liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After both readings of the רישא fail, the גמרא shifts to the סיפא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי שמעון refers to the סיפא and holds that שחיטה done outside is exempt.

steps.title: Rejected again: his wording would have said 'not liable'
steps.stepSummary: This reading also extends an exemption, so רבי שמעון would have said 'anything one is not liable for.' His actual wording does not fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then he should have said 'anything one is not liable for'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the third suggestion for the same kind of reason as step 10. The next step tries one more reading of the סיפא, this time one that extends liability.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here too the model case is an exemption (שחיטה inside), so the rule would need to begin 'כל שאין חייבין.' רבי שמעון's rule says 'כל שחייבין.' So he must be extending liability, from a case that is liable outside to a matching case done inside.

keyTerms.meaning: This. Here it means: this is what he would have needed to say.

steps.whatToRemember: The rule that runs through all the rejections: רבי שמעון's words, 'anything one is liable for outside,' show that his model is a liable outside case, and that he adds liability to a matching inside case. None of the three suggested readings fits that pattern.
steps.confusionAlert: The rejection does not argue about the law itself. It only shows that רבי שמעון's exact wording points in a different direction.

phrases.english: This [should have been]: 'anything one is not liable for'
phrases.notes: This is the short form. He means 'anything one is not liable for when done inside.'

phrases.english: he should have said!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי כֹּל שֶׁאֵין חַיָּיבִין מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The reading that רבי שמעון exempts שחיטה done outside
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: His rule speaks of liability, not exemption.

steps.title: Maybe רבי שמעון extends liability for slaughtering a bird inside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי שמעון is reacting to the first part of the סיפא. Just as one who slaughters a bird outside and offers it outside is liable, one who slaughters it inside and offers it outside would also be liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, maybe he means this: just as one is liable when the bird was slaughtered outside, one is also liable when it was slaughtered inside?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes a new attempt to explain רבי שמעון. This time it reads him as extending liability, which fits his wording 'anything one is liable for outside.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 10 and 12 failed because those readings extended an exemption, and his wording speaks of liability. So now the גמרא flips direction. רבי שמעון would be taking the liability for a bird slaughtered outside and applying it to a bird slaughtered inside.

phrases.english: Rather, just as when it was slaughtered outside he is liable,
so too when it was slaughtered inside he is liable?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the exemption readings fail on wording, the גמרא offers a liability reading from the סיפא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי שמעון makes one who slaughters a bird inside and offers it outside liable, like one who slaughters it outside.

steps.title: רבי שמעון himself exempts a bird slaughtered inside
steps.stepSummary: This reading is rejected. רבי שמעון's own statement ends with 'except for one who slaughters inside and offers up outside,' so he clearly exempts that case.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he teaches: 'except for one who slaughters inside and offers up outside!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the reading from Step 13 by pointing to the end of רבי שמעון's own words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 had רבי שמעון making the inside-slaughtered bird liable. His statement in the משנה names exactly that case as an exception. So he cannot be the one making it liable.

keyTerms.meaning: But it teaches (pointing to the text as a contradiction)
One who offers up on an altar

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two meanings of חוּץ. In 'חוּץ מִן' it means 'except for.' In 'בַּחוּץ' it means 'outside' the courtyard.

phrases.english: But it teaches:
except for one who slaughters a bird inside
and offers it up outside!
phrases.notes: This is the very end of רבי שמעון's statement, so he says this case is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the Step 13 reading.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The reading that רבי שמעון makes an inside-slaughtered bird liable.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It contradicts the exception at the end of רבי שמעון's own statement.

steps.title: זעירי: the argument is about slaughtering an animal at night
steps.stepSummary: זעירי says the argument is about a case the משנה does not spell out: slaughtering an animal at night. On his reading the תנא קמא says that slaughtering inside at night and offering outside is exempt. Slaughtering outside at night and offering outside is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: זעירי said: the difference between them is slaughtering an animal at night. This is what the משנה means: and likewise, one who slaughters an animal inside at night and offers it outside is exempt. One who slaughtered it outside at night and offered it outside is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: Every reading built only on the cases in the משנה has failed. זעירי now says there is an extra case the תנא קמא meant: an animal slaughtered at night. That gives רבי שמעון something to argue about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Slaughtering at night inside disqualifies the animal, so the תנא קמא exempts one who later offers it outside. If the night slaughter happened outside, offering it outside is still liable. This sets up a clear inside-versus-outside difference for רבי שמעון to respond to.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them (this is where they argue)
And this is what it means (reading the text a certain way)

phrases.english: זעירי said:
Slaughtering an animal at night is the difference between them.
And this is what the משנה is saying:
And likewise, one who slaughters an animal inside at night
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording; it shows this case joins the תנא קמא's list.

phrases.english: and offered it up outside is exempt.
If he slaughtered it outside at night
and offered it up outside, he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר זְעֵירִי: שְׁחִיטַת בְּהֵמָה בַּלַּיְלָה אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After all the readings from the משנה's own cases are rejected, זעירי adds a case the משנה does not spell out.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adding a case the משנה leaves unstated (reading the משנה as including it)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון must be reacting to one of the cases written in the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: He is reacting to an unstated case, an animal slaughtered at night, which the תנא קמא exempts when the slaughter was inside.

steps.title: רבי שמעון's words reread on זעירי's approach
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא repeats רבי שמעון's statement and reads it on זעירי's approach. The night slaughter outside brings liability, so a similar slaughter inside followed by offering outside also brings liability. A bird slaughtered inside is the one exception.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: anything one is liable for outside, one is also liable for something like it done inside and then offered up outside. The exception is one who slaughters a bird inside and offers it up outside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes זעירי's explanation by quoting רבי שמעון again. Now his words fit perfectly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His rule now extends liability from outside to inside, which matches the wording that defeated the readings in Steps 7, 9 and 11. Night slaughter outside brings liability, so night slaughter inside does too. The bird exception no longer clashes, because it is a separate case.
steps.whatToRemember: On זעירי's reading, רבי שמעון takes liability from the outside case and applies it to the same act done inside. The only exception is a bird slaughtered inside.

phrases.english: רבי שמעון says:
Anything one is liable for when done outside,
phrases.notes: On זעירי's reading this means the night slaughter outside from the previous step.

phrases.english: one is also liable for the same kind of act done inside
and then offered up outside,
except for one who slaughters a bird inside
and offered it up outside.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: כֹּל שֶׁחַיָּיבִין עָלָיו בַּחוּץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes זעירי's reading by applying רבי שמעון's words to the night-slaughter case.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי שמעון makes one who slaughters an animal inside at night and offers it outside liable, because the same act outside brings liability.

steps.title: רבא: the argument is about collecting blood in a non-sacred vessel
steps.stepSummary: רבא suggests a different unstated case: collecting the blood in an ordinary, non-sacred vessel. The תנא קמא says that collecting inside and offering outside is exempt. Collecting outside and offering outside is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: the difference between them is collecting the blood in a non-sacred vessel. This is what the משנה means: and likewise, one who collects the blood in a non-sacred vessel inside and offers it up outside is exempt. One who collects it in a non-sacred vessel outside and offers it up outside is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second answer, built like זעירי's but with a different case. The disagreement is about collecting blood in a vessel that is not holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Collecting blood in a non-sacred vessel inside disqualifies the offering, so the תנא קמא exempts one who later offers it outside. Done outside, offering it is still liable. On this reading רבי שמעון again extends that liability to the inside case.

keyTerms.meaning: Collecting the blood of the offering
An ordinary vessel, not made holy for Temple use

steps.whatToRemember: זעירי and רבא share the same structure. The תנא קמא exempts when the disqualifying act was done inside, and רבי שמעון makes it liable. They differ only in which disqualifying act it is: slaughter at night, or collecting blood in a non-sacred vessel.

phrases.english: רבא said:
Collecting the blood in a non-sacred vessel is the difference between them.
And this is what the משנה is saying:
And likewise, one who collects the blood in a non-sacred vessel inside
and offered it up outside is exempt.
One who collects the blood in a non-sacred vessel outside
and offered it up outside is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: קַבָּלָה בִּכְלִי חוֹל אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second unstated case, parallel to זעירי's.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adding a different case the משנה leaves unstated
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון must be reacting to one of the cases written in the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The unstated case is collecting blood in a non-sacred vessel, and רבי שמעון makes the inside case liable.

steps.title: Reading רבי שמעון's statement on רבא's approach
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא repeats רבי שמעון's words and reads them on רבא's approach. Collecting blood in an ordinary vessel outside brings liability, so doing the same inside and then offering outside also brings liability. A bird slaughtered inside is the one exception.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: Anything that makes one liable when done outside also makes one liable when a similar act is done inside and the offering is then brought up outside. The exception is one who slaughters a bird inside and offers it up outside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads רבי שמעון's statement again, this time to show how it fits רבא's case of collecting blood in an ordinary vessel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On רבא's approach, the תנא קמא exempts collecting in an ordinary vessel inside and then offering outside. רבי שמעון disagrees: since collecting this way outside brings liability, doing it inside should too. He agrees only that slaughtering a bird inside and offering it outside is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: something similar to it, the same kind of act
and he offered it up (on an altar)

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
Anything for which one is liable when done outside,
one is also liable for something similar to it
done inside, when he then offered it up outside,
phrases.notes: On רבא's reading, the 'similar act' is collecting the blood in an ordinary, non-sacred vessel.

phrases.english: except for one who slaughters a bird
inside and offers it up outside.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: כֹּל שֶׁחַיָּיבִין עָלָיו בַּחוּץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבא's proposed case to רבי שמעון's words, just as step 16 did for זעירי's case.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: On רבא's reading, רבי שמעון holds that collecting in an ordinary vessel inside and then offering outside brings liability. Only a bird slaughtered inside is exempt.

steps.title: A ברייתא about pinching a bird's neck
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא taught by the father of שמואל בר רב יצחק. Pinching a bird inside and offering it outside brings liability. Pinching it outside and offering it outside is exempt. רבי שמעון holds that one is liable in that second case too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that the father of שמואל בר רב יצחק has taught a ברייתא: One who pinches a bird inside and offers it up outside is liable. One who pinched it outside and offered it up outside is exempt. And רבי שמעון holds him liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source that shows exactly where רבי שמעון disagrees. This sets up a new way to read his statement in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bird pinched outside is not a proper קרבן, so the תנא קמא says offering it outside is exempt. The ברייתא states openly that רבי שמעון holds one is liable even there. That tells us which case his statement is really about.

keyTerms.meaning: one who pinches the back of a bird's neck (מליקה)

phrases.english: Now that he has taught
the father of Shmuel bar Rav Yitzḥak:
One who pinches a bird inside
and offers it up outside is liable;
if he pinched outside and offered it up outside, he is exempt;
and Rabbi Shimon holds him liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא דְּתָנֵי אֲבוּהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Instead of looking for an unstated case like זעירי and רבא did, the גמרא brings an explicit ברייתא. It shows that רבי שמעון argues on the pinching case suggested in step 7.
steps.raayaObject: Which case רבי שמעון is disagreeing about in the משנה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of the father of שמואל בר רב יצחק, which says רבי שמעון holds one liable for pinching outside and offering outside

steps.title: רבי שמעון is reacting to the pinching case
steps.stepSummary: Based on the ברייתא, the גמרא says רבי שמעון is reacting to the earlier pinching case, and his words should be read in reverse order. Whatever brings liability when done inside and then offered outside also brings liability when done outside and offered outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון is standing on that case, so read his words this way: Anything for which one is liable when done inside and then offered up outside, one is also liable for when done outside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles where רבי שמעון's words belong and changes their wording to match.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה made pinching inside and offering outside liable, and pinching outside and offering outside exempt. רבי שמעון says the outside case should match the inside case, so both are liable. This is the same reading the גמרא tried in step 7, which was rejected in step 8 only because of the wording; the ברייתא shows it is right, so the גמרא changes the wording to begin with 'בפנים'.

keyTerms.meaning: he is standing on (reacting to) that case

steps.whatToRemember: The final reading: רבי שמעון reacts to the pinching case. Since pinching inside and offering outside brings liability, pinching outside and offering outside brings liability too.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon is referring to there,
phrases.notes: 'There' means the earlier case in the משנה of pinching a bird's neck.

phrases.english: so read it this way:
Anything for which one is liable when done inside
and then he offered it up outside,
one is also liable for it when done outside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the ברייתא in step 19. It brings back the step 7 reading and fixes the wording problem raised in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning the statement to a different clause and reordering its wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The reading that רבי שמעון argues on the pinching case (step 7) was rejected because his rule begins 'כל שחייבין עליו בחוץ', not 'בפנים' (step 8).
steps.terutzMaskana: He is reacting to the pinching case: an act done outside matches the same act done inside, so both bring liability.

steps.title: משנה: blood of a חטאת collected in one cup
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה teaches that if the blood of a חטאת was collected in one cup and placed both outside and inside, in either order, one is liable. All of the blood in that cup is fit to be placed inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A חטאת whose blood was collected in one cup: if he placed some outside and then placed some inside, or placed some inside and then some outside, he is liable, because all of it is fit to be placed inside.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It rules on a חטאת whose blood is all in one cup and is placed partly outside the עזרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even after some blood was placed inside, the rest of the same cup is still fit for the inside altar. So placing it outside is offering fit blood outside, and he is liable whichever placement came first.

keyTerms.meaning: our משנה (a new משנה starts here)
cup, a vessel for collecting blood
since all of it is fit to be placed inside

steps.confusionAlert: Even when the inside placement came first, he is still liable for the outside one. With one cup, the rest of the blood stays fit.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A sin offering whose blood he collected
in one cup:
if he placed it outside and then placed it inside,
or inside and then placed it outside,
he is liable, as all of it is fit to be placed inside.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ חַטָּאת שֶׁקִּבֵּל דָּמָהּ בְּכוֹס אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With blood in one cup, placing any of it outside brings liability in either order, because all of it is fit to be placed inside.

steps.title: משנה: blood of a חטאת collected in two cups
steps.stepSummary: When the blood was collected in two cups, the order matters. Both inside is exempt. Both outside is liable. Inside first and then outside is exempt. Outside first and then inside is liable for the outside placement, and the inside placement still atones.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he collected its blood in two cups: placing both inside is exempt; placing both outside is liable; placing one inside and then one outside is exempt; placing one outside and then one inside makes him liable for the outside one, and the inside one atones.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with a חטאת whose blood was split into two cups, and goes through each possible order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the first cup is placed inside, the מצוה is done and the second cup is no longer fit, so placing it outside does not bring liability. If the outside cup comes first, the inside cup was still fit at that moment, so he is liable. The later inside placement still brings atonement.
steps.whatToRemember: One cup: placing any blood outside brings liability, in either order. Two cups: inside first exempts the outside placement. Outside first brings liability, and the inside placement still atones.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that liability for offering outside depends on whether the blood was still fit for the inside altar at the moment it was placed outside.

phrases.english: If he collected its blood in two cups:
if he placed both of them inside, he is exempt.
If both were placed outside, he is liable.
If one was placed inside and then one outside, he is exempt.
If one was placed outside and then one inside,
he is liable for the outer placement,
and the inner placement atones.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה, moving from one cup to two cups.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With two cups, inside first exempts the later outside placement. Outside first brings liability, and the inside placement still atones.

steps.title: Setting up a comparison: two animals for one חטאת
steps.stepSummary: The משנה compares the two-cups case to a person who now has two animals set aside for one חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is this like? It is like a person who set aside an animal as his חטאת and it got lost. He set aside another one in its place, and then the first one was found. Now both are standing in front of him.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is setting up a comparison. It describes a case where a person ends up with two animals for one חטאת, and the next step will give the rulings for that case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the two-cups case, there are two portions of blood but only one obligation. The lost-and-found case has the same shape: two animals, both fit, but only one is needed. By describing this familiar case, the משנה shows that the blood rule is not new. It follows a pattern we already know.

keyTerms.meaning: To what is this matter comparable? (introduces a comparison)
one who sets aside an animal for a קרבן
in its place, as a replacement

phrases.english: To what is this matter comparable?
To one who separated his sin offering and it was lost,
and he separated another in its place,
and afterward the first one was found,
and now both of them are standing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces a parallel case to explain the two-cups rulings of Step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The two-cups case is like a person who has two fit animals set aside for one חטאת.

steps.title: The four outcomes for slaughtering the two animals
steps.stepSummary: Both inside is exempt. Both outside is liable. Inside then outside is exempt. Outside then inside is liable for the outside one, and the inside one still atones.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he slaughtered both inside, he is exempt. If he slaughtered both outside, he is liable. If he slaughtered one inside and then one outside, he is exempt. If he slaughtered one outside and then one inside, he is liable for the outside one, and the inside one gives him atonement.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the rulings for the two-animal case. They match the four rulings for the two cups of blood exactly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key idea is whether the second animal was still fit when it was slaughtered outside. Once one animal is brought inside, the obligation is done and the other is no longer fit, so slaughtering it outside brings no liability. But if the outside one came first, it was still fit to be brought inside, so he is liable for it, and the inside one that follows still counts.

keyTerms.meaning: liable (here, for slaughtering a קרבן outside)

steps.whatToRemember: Order matters. Whatever happens first, while both are still fit, decides things. Outside before inside means liable. Inside before outside means exempt.
steps.confusionAlert: In "one inside and one outside" he is exempt only because the inside one came first. Do not read it as "any mix of inside and outside is exempt." The reverse order is liable.

phrases.english: If he slaughtered both of them inside, he is exempt.
Both of them outside, he is liable.
One inside and then one outside, he is exempt.
One outside and then one inside:
he is liable for the outside one,
and the inside one atones.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the rulings for the comparison case set up in Step 23, matching Step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With two animals for one חטאת: both inside is exempt; both outside is liable; inside then outside is exempt; outside then inside is liable for the outside one, and the inside one atones.

steps.title: One animal's blood exempts the partner's meat too
steps.stepSummary: When both were slaughtered inside, placing the blood of one exempts its own meat and also the meat of the other animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as its blood exempts its own meat, so too it exempts the meat of its partner.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds one more rule to the two-animal case. Placing the blood of one animal affects the meat of the second animal as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, once the blood of a קרבן is placed on the מזבח, someone who eats its meat is no longer liable for מעילה. The משנה says the same blood also frees the partner animal's meat. Both animals were set aside for one obligation, so when one finishes the job, it ends the holy status of the other in this respect too.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the two animals are treated as one unit for one obligation. What one accomplishes affects the other.

phrases.english: Just as its blood exempts its own meat,
phrases.notes: "Exempts" means someone who eats the meat is no longer liable for מעילה.

phrases.aramaic: כָּךְ הִיא פּוֹטֶרֶת אֶת בְּשַׂר חֲבֶירְתָּהּ.
phrases.english: so too it exempts the meat of its counterpart.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further rule about the meat in the two-animal case from Steps 23-24.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When both animals were slaughtered inside, the blood of one exempts both its own meat and its partner's meat from מעילה.
